summary: Social AI chat app where people and bots share group conversations.
editor_note: The interesting choice is putting AI inside a shared conversation, not asking everyone to open a private chatbot. Shapes documents a simple loop: start a chat, invite friends, and add characters with their own backstories and response styles. Free engines coexist with credit-funded premium engines, so the model catalog is not an all-free promise. The hard part is moderation: social AI gets more interesting exactly where it gets harder to keep safe.

sources.label: Shapes introduction and engine pricing boundaries

product_evidence.claim: The chat guide shows users starting a conversation from New Chat, then using Members / Invite to add people, add AI characters, or share an invitation link.
The character creation guide exposes backstory and response-style settings, with optional personality traits, tone, and example conversations before publishing a Shape.
Shapes documents chats containing humans and AI characters together, with up to five Shapes active at once.
The documentation distinguishes free engines from premium engines that consume Shape Credits; credits can be purchased or earned, and a free engine remains available for chatting.

market_context.primary_user: Consumers and character creators who want shared chats with friends and AI personalities, including fandom and roleplay groups.
market_context.differentiation: Human participants and configurable AI characters share the same conversation; invitations and character creation are part of the chat workflow rather than separate chatbot sessions.
market_context.why_now: The April 2026 seed announcement and published chat, character, and credit guides give concrete checkpoints for tracking how the social AI format develops.

risks.claim: The hard part is moderation: social AI gets more interesting exactly where it gets harder to keep safe.
risks.basis: VentureDex editorial assessment of mixed human-AI group conversations; this review did not test moderation or safety outcomes.

risks.claim: Actual premium-engine costs and safe behavior across different characters remain questions for account-level testing; public documentation alone does not establish either.
risks.basis: The documentation describes credit-funded engines and user-configured characters; no account, paid credits, or live group chat was tested in this review.

risks.claim: Founding-year accounts conflict, so this profile does not assert a year. Its investor list is limited to the verified lead investor, not a complete cap table.
risks.basis: Official launch and TechCrunch founding years differ; the official seed announcement confirms Lightspeed as lead but not all investors previously listed here.
